chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Attiyah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The dawn is that which, when you see it crossing [the sky], resembles the whiteness of the river of Sura."

key_terms.الْفَجْرُ: Dawn, the time of the Fajr prayer
key_terms.مُعْتَرِضاً: Crossing horizontally, extending across the sky
key_terms.نَهْرِ سُورَاءَ: River of Sura, a reference to a specific geographical or meteorological phenomenon used as a visual benchmark

ai.seo_question: How to identify the exact time of dawn for fasting according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between the false dawn (Al-Fajr al-Kadhib), which rises vertically and dissipates quickly, and the true dawn (Al-Fajr al-Sadiq), which appears horizontally and remains until sunrise. The Imam’s analogy to the 'whiteness of the river Sura' provides a tangible visual benchmark for laypeople to accurately determine the onset of the fasting period, a critical detail in Shia fiqh for ensuring the validity of daily prayers and fasting.
